tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

# v0.1 reconstruction: corpus brief

Read first: `SP/v01/kernel-brief.md` (context, hard rules), `SP/v01/arena-ref-brief.md`,
`SP/v01/lib-brief.md`, `SP/v01/arbitration.md` (Q19–Q23 and the two follow-up answers), and the phase
reports `SP/v01/kernel-report.md`, `SP/v01/arena-report.md`, `SP/v01/lib-report.md`.
`SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref`.
Material: `~/Downloads/ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md` (v2), `~/Downloads/ERN_MM-03.3_v0.4_pour_validation.md`,
`~/Downloads/Derivability_v0.1.md` are local inputs: never commit or copy them into the repository.

Brief obligation 7 (unchanged): each case gives a state reached from the initial state, the expected
verdict from its source, a positive twin for each rejection, and a class. No case is corrected or
bypassed, except as the user arbitrated (Q19, Q21 below). MM2-H is already done (H01 twin = the
write-then-read variant, H10 = the access leaving the allocation; `Corpus/MM2H.lean`).

## Expected verdicts under v0.1

- A case's expected verdict comes from its source. Where v0.1 changes the verdict a source gave under
  v0 (amended clauses: §36, §40, §47, §51, §57, §59, §60.1, §63.4, §63.9, §69.2, §70.3, §71.2, §74,
  §75, §76.6, §78.3, §82.2, §86; contracts HandlePool v0.5 and DS-v2), record in the docstring: the
  historical expected verdict, its justification, the new expected verdict and the v0.1 clause or
  contract item that decides it. Derive the new expected verdict from the v0.1 text, never from the
  obtained outcome. Collect every such case in the table of your report (columns: case, historical
  verdict, justification, new verdict, deciding clause, obtained).
- Q21 decisions: H21, H50, H51: new verdict = obtained. H49: regression test, verdict = obtained,
  residual blocking documented (NoLock decision, §65 last paragraph); its rejected `reset` is exempt
  from a positive twin. H16: classified Spec 3 (inter-spec obligation, non-blocking). W2 and W3: the
  variants become the cases. W1: the value is removed before `freeSlot`, along the path of the Q3
  witness (resolve Modify, write, transfer of the entry to a local, unresolve, freeSlot). Re-evaluate
  W2 under the §63.4 exemption (follow-up answer) and record the outcome.
- Q19: H31a's multi-step twin (conjunct 5) is the accepted twin.
- Q20: MM23-H14 (Spec 3) and MM23-H17 (Specs 4 and 11) are classified non-blocking, not encoded.
- Q22: H13a, H13b, MM23-H04, MM23-H13, H10 formation are open boundaries, non-blocking; `exitRoots`
  is the reference realization for MM23-H09.
- Section J of MM3-H stays unencoded and classified.
- `pool_free_entry_handle`: under HandlePool v0.5 and Q12, `fail`. DS03 and DS05: decided by DS-v2.

## Files and protocol

- Runner agent first: `Corpus/Runner.lean`, `Corpus/LibRunner.lean` (executors; adapt to the new APIs:
  `unpin` on an obligation identity, `K.ExternalDone` on obligation identities, new preconditions,
  HandlePool v0.5 and DS-v2 steps). May run `lake build` of these two modules.
- Then in parallel, one agent per file, `lake env lean` only: `Corpus/MM3H.lean`, `Corpus/MM23H.lean`,
  `Corpus/Lib.lean`, `Corpus/DataStack.lean`.
- Every case theorem re-proved; every mismatch (obtained ≠ expected under v0.1) reported with its
  class: case defect, spec defect or module defect. A module defect is not fixed in the corpus phase:
  report it.
- Module headers cite the v0.1 file.

import Ern.Corpus.Runner

/-!
# Corpus MM3-H: access discipline, sections A–F, H, I (test module)

The cases of corpus MM3-H of the Jalon 3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`, §1; non-normative
design material), run on the reference kernel and arena of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` (§60–§78), plus new cases fixed by spec clauses and
the usage scenario W3 (material §5b). This is a test module: no model module imports it.

Each case is a run from `LState.init statics` (§47) by the runner (`Ern.Corpus.Runner`):
`RunsTo k statics os L` states that every step is `ok` and that `L` is library-reachable and its
kernel state `Reachable` (§57). The verdict of the step under test is stated with the relation of
its operation (`DeriveStep`, `TransferStep`, `IssueD`, `ResetD`, …) on the reached state and
decided by `decide`. Each docstring gives the expected verdict from the case's source (the
material, or the spec clause for new cases), the obtained verdict, the class (material §0, rule 5:
`N3` kernel, `Lib` library instance, `spec 3` another specification) and the positive twin (rule 2:
the same sequence without the faulty element, accepted). A case whose obtained verdict differs from
the expected one is kept with its expected verdict and marked **MISMATCH** with its cause; no case
is corrected. Where spec v0.1 or an arbitration of the corpus owner changes the expected verdict a
case had under spec v0 (H21, H49, H50, H51), its docstring gives the historical expected verdict,
its justification, the new expected verdict and the v0.1 clause that decides it; H16 gives the
same history for its spec v0 mismatch, which v0.1 closes.

Twins that are not literally the same sequence without one faulty step:
* another destination, target, parameter or identity in place of the faulty one: H04 (the other
  element), H13 (`z`), H18 (the local leaf 3), H21 (a `Modify` parameter), H25 (a `Modify`
  parameter on the static), H29 (a `Modify` parameter), H50 `transfer` (the stored authority on
  the local 4), H50 `issue` (the value 2), H51 direct form (the view on `u`), S63_8 (the stored
  authority on the local 6), S56 (`internal` 5), S77_2 (the destination 3 outside the region,
  `fail`; the available region `[6]`, `ok`);
* further steps that lift the blocking before the step under test: H11 (`endUse` of `v2` and of
  the leaf 6), H17 (`endUse` of the block value, then `free` of the storage 4 instead of the leaf
  5), H19 (`endUse` of the child value), H26 second twin (the contract with `ExternalDone` on the
  obligation, then `unpin`), H27b (three `release`), W3 (`endUse` of the structure);
* a pairing given by the material: H05 (its own twin), H21b (H37);
* a faulty element of several steps, removed: H03, S77_6 (`derive` and `store`), H16 (the `free`),
  H51 through a helper (the view, or its `store`), H49 `endUse` of the block values (the six steps
  of the cycle);
* no twin, by arbitration: the `reset` `reject` in the state `h49` of H49, which persists without
  the cycle (on `fao` the blocks are still held by the values 2 and 3, §78.2).

Local shapes are lists of (parent, kind) (§72, §71.1); `lf` is a root leaf, `pt p` a part of `p`.
Place and authority identities are list indices (§38): `enterFrame` appends the locals and one
root authority per root local; `alloc` appends the shape and one root authority; `derive` and
`split` append the derived authorities; `issue` appends one block authority; `reset` appends one
(released) authority.

Not encoded here:
* section G (H30–H34b, H44, handle pools) and the usage scenarios W1, W2 (they use a handle pool):
  `Ern.Corpus.Lib`;
* the cross-registry cases of §56 (a pool and an arena, or two pools, on one `internal`):
  `Ern.Corpus.Lib`; only the arena registry exists here (`S56`);
* section J, out of the kernel, classified by the material: H38 get-or-insert cache (spec 3,
  flow-sensitive liveness, §25, §32); H39 suspended coroutine holding a `Modify` parameter
  (specs 2 and 3, §29, §81); H40 raw pointer used during a call (spec 3 and the boundary of §19,
  §81); H41 concurrent `writeShared` (spec 2, §18, §24, §68); H42 `defer free(x)` then

-/
------
theorem H15 : RunsTo KF2 [] h15o h15 ∧ FreeStep KF2 2 7 h15.kern .reject ∧
    Runs KF2 [] (h14p ++ [.alloc 0 2 [lf], .free 2 7]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Test contract of H16 (§70.2, §80): place 3 deallocable by the authority 7. -/
abbrev KF3 : K := KD.toK { dealloc := [3], compat := [(3, 7)] }

/-- Prefix of H16 (§72, §71, §60): frame 1 with allocator 0, `x` (1) and the result `R` (2);
storage 3 owned by `x`, written; parameters 4 (`Modify` on `x`) and 5 (`Modify` on `R`) passed to
frame 2, which has the local 4. -/
def h16p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .alloc 0 1 [lf],
  .write 3 [3], .derive 1 [1] .modify, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf]]
/-- State reached by `h16p` (§57). -/
def h16a : LState := final KF3 [] h16p
/-- Run of H16 (§63, §70, §73): the callee receives `x` by `transfer` into its local 4, frees the
storage 3 now owned by that local, returns the value by `transfer` into `R` through the parameter
5, then exits. -/
def h16o : List Op := h16p ++ [.transfer 1 4, .free 3 7, .transfer 4 2, .exit]
/-- State reached by `h16o` (§57). -/
def h16 : LState := final KF3 [] h16o

convention of Spec 3, §45, §81; non-blocking). The callee receives by transfer a value owning a
storage, frees it, returns the value; the caller reads that storage. Expected (material): `ok`,
then `reject`. Historical (spec v0): same expected verdict; the reception, `transfer` of `x` into
the callee's local, was obtained `reject`, the parameter 4 being an active derived authority
covering `x` held outside it (§63.4 before its v0.1 amendment); **MISMATCH**, case defect. Spec
v0.1 decides the reception `ok`: the parameter 4 is the exercisable authority on which the
`Modify` right over `x` rests, exempt from the check with its origin chain (v0.1 §63.4); the
expected verdict, unchanged, is now the spec's and the mismatch is closed. Obtained: the
reception, the `free` of the storage through the callee's local (§70), the return into `R` (§63)
and the exit (§73) are `ok`; the caller's read of the storage is `reject` for every authority
(§66.1: the leaf belongs to no usable place, §70 effect). Twin without the `free`: the read is

# User arbitrations of the blocking report (verbatim, French)

Arbitrages (rapport bloquant, section 7) :

Q1 : (b). Ajouter à §63 « la destination est utilisable dans l'état d'arrivée ».
Q2 : lecture mixte sur l'état d'arrivée : invariants du noyau sur l'état entier, plus ArenaInv de la nouvelle entrée ; NewArenaBase porte cette lecture.
Q3 : réalisation par des pas du noyau. freeSlot (contrat HandlePool v0.5) marque l'entrée libre et incrémente la génération ; préconditions : droit d'administration, pool vivant, handle valide, aucune feuille de l'entrée à Init (Uninit ou Moved), aucune autorité active dérivée d'une compagne de ce pool sur l'entrée ; aucun effet d'endUse. Deux preuves obligatoires :
  (1) témoin complet depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés : newPool, allocSlot, resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de la valeur vers un local de même forme, unresolve, freeSlot accepté ;
  (2) la mise à jour des métadonnées (état libre, génération) est réalisable par une écriture autorisée sous le droit d'administration.
Q4 : garantie par pool : réécrire D.2, D.3 et D.4(3) sur les compagnes du pool du slot ; les pools imbriqués restent permis ; I1 et les garanties du noyau restent prouvées sur l'état entier.
Q5 : la validation du handle précède le contrôle du droit : fail dans les deux cas.
Q6 : réécrire §86 s4 : « La réémission ne modifie ni les octets ni l'état d'initialisation. Une lecture reste soumise aux conditions ordinaires du modèle mémoire, notamment Init, aux droits d'accès et à la validité de représentation pour le type demandé. La Spec 4 déterminera les obligations de construction et de typage des valeurs réémises. »
Q7 : restreindre §78.3 aux ancres du sous-arbre strict de internal qui couvrent une feuille du stockage administré ; prouver que la clause découle de §78.2 et de I3 (lecture Q9), et l'équivalence de reset avec sa séquence du noyau dans les deux sens.
Q8 : ajouter à §47 : le graphe de possession des statiques est acyclique.
Q9 et Q26 : « valide » = active. §69.2 : endUse est rejeté si une autorité détenue par place a un descendant actif détenu ailleurs.
Q10 : (a).
Q11 : (a) fail ; (b) reject ; (c) reject ; (d) mark exige AdminRight ; (e) grow suit le détenteur actuel du bloc ; (f) fail avant le contrôle du droit (contrat DS-v2).
Q12 : avec le nouveau freeSlot, un handle d'entrée libre est périmé : fail.
Q13 : §71.2 inchangé ; préciser au §36 que MetaRight vise la création ou le recyclage d'autorités sur un stockage existant, pas la création d'une allocation fraîche par alloc ; la concurrence entre appels relève de la spec 2.
Q14 : « opérations d'accès » = O9–O11 ; le préciser au §59.
Q15 : restreindre §40 aux emplacements racines utilisables, comme §49.7.
Q16 : définir I5 : toute feuille épinglée appartient à un emplacement utilisable.
Q17 : lecture actuelle.
Q18 : région dont toutes les feuilles sont de taille nulle : base et provenance de l'allocation de l'ancre effective, comme la région vide.
Q19 : H31a : le jumeau à plusieurs pas (conjonct 5) est accepté.
Q20 : non bloquants (classés).

Q25 : (b).
Q27 : (a).
Q28 : (c) fail (une pile morte invalide ses marques).

Spec : ne pas modifier `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md`. Créer `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` à partir de la v0, avec les amendements Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9/Q26, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q24 et B#45 (§74, §75), en anglais ; en-tête : « Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated », suivi de la liste des clauses modifiées. Commit séparé `docs(specs): add memory model v0.1 corrective candidate`. La reconstruction suit la v0.1.
Contrats locaux : HandlePool v0.5 (Q3, Q4, Q5, Q12) et DS-v2 (Q11, Q27, Q28), changements listés dans la description de PR.
Preuves : refaire celles qui sont touchées ; les garanties de Q1, Q3, Q7 et B#45 sont démontrées sur les états atteignables du contrat, sans hypothèse supplémentaire non normative ; tout échec de preuve est rapporté, jamais contourné. Ouvrir la PR si la condition du brief est remplie.

## Follow-up answers (verbatim, French)

Q9 (suite) : règle unifiée. endUse et free sont rejetés si une autorité qu'ils désactivent — détenue par un emplacement qui meurt, stockage possédé transitivement compris, ou racine d'un stockage libéré — a un descendant actif, quelle que soit son empreinte, que le même pas ne désactive pas. Les cas (1) et (2) sont donc rejetés. La sortie de cadre garde son ré-ancrage, et rejette si aucune origine survivante n'existe (inchangé). I2 au sens « origine active » tient après chaque pas.

Q3 (suite) : remplace Q17. Dans §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3, sont exemptées des contrôles « autorité dérivée active couvrant depuis l'extérieur » les autorités par lesquelles le pas exerce son droit Modify : l'autorité exerçable qui fonde le droit et sa chaîne d'origines (pour le pool : entrée, compagne, internal et ses origines). Les autres autorités actives restent contrôlées. Le témoin Q3 (1) devient : resolve Modify, écriture, transfer de l'entrée vers un local, unresolve, freeSlot accepté, y compris avec internal dérivé. W1 suit le même chemin. Réévaluer W2 sous cette lecture. Ajouter §63.4, §69.2 et §70.3 aux amendements de la v0.1.

(Cases (1) and (2) above refer to: (1) endUse(p) where p owns an allocation q holding a stored authority a, the frame holding b derived from a over another static; (2) free(p) with an empty-footprint derivative of p's root held by the frame.)

import Ern.Corpus.Runner
import Ern.MemoryModel.RefinementArena

/-!
# Corpus MM23-H: refinement (test module)

The cases of corpus MM23-H of the Jalon 3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`, §3; non-normative
design material), replayed on the reference refinement of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` (§82, Part XIV). This is a test module: no model or
library module imports it.

Each case is a run from the initial state (§47) translated into the elementary memory machine with
the contract, the deallocation compatibility (equality of tokens), the read and write obligations
and the parameters fixed once for the run (§20.3 ¶3, §82): the test layout `piOf` of
`Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement.Runs` (each root place in its own allocation, each leaf 8 bytes at 8
times its rank, `LayoutWF` established by `Repr`), the placement `topPlacement`, the tokens
`100 + r`, the 8-byte reference encoding `pe8`. Runs of kernel operations only are kernel
simulation runs (`SimRun`, built by `srun`, conclusions by `simulation`); runs with an arena are
library simulation runs (`LSimRun`, built by the runner `lsrun` below, conclusions by
`lsimulation`), in which `issue` is the derived library operation (`split` then `store`) and
`reset` the derived reset (`derive` then `release`). The reached states are those of these runs
(material §0, rule 3). The obtained result is stated with the kernel relation of the step under
test, the machine relations of its realized raw operations (`ReadStep`, `WriteStep`,
`DeallocStep`, `Exec`) and the bytes read back, all decided by `decide`.

Each docstring gives the expected verdict of the material, the obtained one, the class (material
§0, rule 5: `R` refinement) and the positive twin of each rejection or `fail` (rule 2). A case
whose obtained verdict differs from its expected one, or whose expected verdict has no spec v0.1
source, is kept with its expected verdict and classified; no case is corrected. No expected
verdict of this corpus changes under v0.1.

Address rules of references (`Refinement.ptrAddr`): a region whose leaves all have zero physical
size, the empty region included, has the base of the allocation of the effective anchor of its
authority, with that allocation as provenance (§82.2, last sentence); a region with a leaf of
nonzero size has the lowest address among its leaves of nonzero size (a decision of the
reconstruction recorded for §82.3, not stated by v0.1); the destination leaf has the size of a
reference (`pe8.size = 8`).

Not encoded (classified, material §3 and §6; non-blocking by the user's arbitration Q20):
* MM23-H14, a raw pointer formed before a call and used during the call on the footprint of a
  `Modify` parameter: undefined behavior that no safe program constructs; class spec 3 (strong
  protection of parameters during the invocation, §72 last paragraph, §81) with the boundary of
  §19 (reconstruction of accesses from raw addresses).
* MM23-H17, a reference stored into a leaf of zero size: a conditional obligation of specs 4 and
  11 (a reference occupies a leaf of pointer size), not a guarantee of the refinement; class
  specs 4 and 11 (§81, §82.3 "a single logical leaf with an appropriate representation"). The
  pointer-size rule is a hypothesis of `Refinement.pointer_sound_store`.

Open boundaries of the spec (non-blocking by arbitration Q22): MM23-H04 and MM23-H13 (propagation
of provenance through copies, §10 ¶4, §19) and MM23-H09 (deallocation of automatic storage at
exit, §9 ¶2, §73), for which `Refinement.exitRoots` is the reference realization.
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.MM23H

open Ern.MemoryModel Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement
  Ern.MemoryModel.RefinementArena Ern.Corpus
open Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement.Runs (piOf piOf_ok obR obW wv decodedAt kernelRun sinit)

/-! ## Test contracts (§48, §80) -/

/-- Test contract (§48): the `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone` (on identities of dynamic
pinning obligations, §75), `Deallocable` and `FreeCompat` lists of a `KD`; `DeclaredDisjoint` is
leaf disjointness (§23) when `dd` holds and declares nothing otherwise; `Satisfiable` (§71) is
`sat` for every request. -/
def KT (d : KD) (dd sat : Bool) : K :=
  ⟨fun r r' => dd = true ∧ ∀ l ∈ r, l ∉ r', (· ∈ d.shared), (· ∈ d.pinned), (· ∈ d.done),
    (· ∈ d.dealloc), fun p a => (p, a) ∈ d.compat, fun _ _ _ => sat = true⟩

/-- Decidability of `DeclaredDisjoint` for a test contract (§48). -/
-----
    lsimOf (KT.ddSound _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

/-! ## Run R6: a region whose head is not its lowest leaf (H16) -/

/-- Run R6 (§72, §67, §71, §76, §77): frame 1 with the arena value 0, the provider 1, the leaf 2;
storage 3 (leaves 4 at offset 0 and 5 at offset 8) owned by 0, its root authority 3 the `internal`
of the arena; the derived `issue` of the region `[5, 4]` to 2 (block 4). -/
def l6 : List LOp := [.kernel (.enter [] [lf, lf, lf]), .kernel (.write 1 [1] wv),
  .kernel (.alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 3, pt 3]), .kernel (.write 0 [0] wv), .newArena [] 3 3,
  .issue 0 [5, 4] 2]

/-- Parameters of R6, fixed once from its final places (§82). -/
def π6 : Params Unit := piOf (placesOf [] l6) []

/-- State of R6 after its first `n` steps (§82.7). -/
def lt6 (n : Nat) : LState × Machine.State := lfin K5 [] π6 (l6.take n)

/-- **MM23-H16** (material §3, class R). Reference to a region whose first listed leaf does not
have the lowest offset. Expected (material): the lowest address among the nonempty leaves.
Obtained: the same; the case passes. R6 is reached (`LSim`), the issue being the derived library
operation, realized by one write of the destination 2. Block 4 has the region `[5, 4]`, recorded
in the arena entry; both leaves have nonzero size, leaf 4 at offset 0 below the head 5 at offset
8; the range of 2 decodes to the address of leaf 4, not to that of the head, every byte with the
storage allocation as provenance. Source of the expected verdict: a decision of the reconstruction
recorded for §82.3 (lowest-address rule), not stated by spec v0.1: §82.2 decides only regions
whose leaves all have zero physical size, and §81 leaves encodings to Spec 11. -/
theorem H16 : LSim K5 [] π6 (lt6 5) ∧ LSim K5 [] π6 (lt6 6) ∧
    (lopsOf π6 (.issue 0 [5, 4] 2) (lt6 5).1 (lt6 5).2).map opKind = [1] ∧
    (lopsOf π6 (.issue 0 [5, 4] 2) (lt6 5).1 (lt6 5).2).map opAlloc = [some (π6.L 2).alloc] ∧
    (lt6 6).1.arenas = [⟨3, 3, [], [([5, 4], 4)]⟩] ∧ (lt6 6).1.kern.afp 4 = [5, 4] ∧
    (π6.L 4).off = 0 ∧ (π6.L 5).off = 8 ∧ 0 < (π6.L 4).len ∧ 0 < (π6.L 5).len ∧
    leafAddr (lt6 6).2 π6.L 4 < leafAddr (lt6 6).2 π6.L 5 ∧
    decodedAt π6 (lt6 6).2 2 = leafAddr (lt6 6).2 π6.L 4 ∧
    decodedAt π6 (lt6 6).2 2 ≠ leafAddr (lt6 6).2 π6.L 5 ∧
    (∀ i < 8, (bytesOf (lt6 6).2 π6.L 2 i).2 = some (π6.L 3).alloc) ∧ (π6.L 2).len = 8 :=
  ⟨lsimOf (KT.ddSound _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide),
    lsimOf (KT.ddSound _ _ _) (by decide) (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide⟩

end Ern.Corpus.MM23H

Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. 3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).

Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). def h21o : List Op := h21p ++ [.derive 0 [0] .observe, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf],
  .writeShared 4 [0]]
/-- State reached by `h21o` (§57). -/
def h21 : LState := final KA [] h21o

/-- **H21** (material §1 D, class Lib). A callee that only observes the arena issues a block to a
local, then returns the block. Historical expected verdict (material): `ok`, which the Jalon 3
draft obtained through a `writeShared` branch of `MetaRight`; under spec v0 the case was a
**MISMATCH** (expected `ok`, obtained `reject`). New expected verdict (spec v0.1, by arbitration
the obtained one): `reject` at the `issue`, decided by §36 and §77.1: `MetaRight` requires
exercisable `Modify` on the arena value and `writeShared` alone does not satisfy it (v0.1 §36 keeps
this rule; its amendment concerns `alloc` only). Obtained: the `writeShared` on the metadata is
`ok` (§68), the `issue` is `reject`. Twin, the same run with a `Modify` parameter on the arena
value: `issue`, `transfer` of the block value to the caller and `exitFrame` are `ok`. -/
theorem H21 : RunsTo KA [] h21o h21 ∧ IssueD KA 0 [4] 6 h21 .reject ∧
    OptP (h21.arenas[0]?) (fun E => ¬ MetaRight h21.kern E) False ∧
    Runs KA [] (h21p ++ [.derive 0 [0] .modify, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf],
      .writeShared 4 [0], .issue 0 [4] 6, .transfer 6 2, .exit]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [4] 6) (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H21b (§72, §60, §65, §76): frame 1 with the result 0 passes 1, `Modify` on it, to
frame 2, which has the arena value 1 and the local buffer 2 (parts 3, 4); the callee derives 4,
`Modify` on the buffer, stores it into the arena value and creates the arena. -/
def h21bo : List Op := [.enter [] [lf], .derive 0 [0] .modify,
  .enter [1] [lf, lf, pt 2, pt 2], .derive 3 [3, 4] .modify, .store 4 1, .newArena 2 4]
----
def h50t : LState := final K0 [] h50to

/-- **H50**, `transfer` part (material §1 I, class N3). An authority transferred into the place
it covers: structure 0 is transferred into structure 2 while its field 1 holds 3, which covers
the field 3 = `corr(1)`. Historical expected verdict (material): to arbitrate; under spec v0 a
**MISMATCH** in form (obtained `reject`). New expected verdict (spec v0.1, by arbitration the
obtained one): `reject`, decided by §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, §88). Obtained: `reject`
by §63.8 alone (§63.1–§63.7 and §63.9 hold). Twin, the stored authority covering the local 4
instead: `ok`. -/
theorem H50_transfer : RunsTo K0 [] h50to h50t ∧ TransferStep K0 0 2 h50t.kern .reject ∧
    TransferPre637 K0 h50t.kern 0 2 ∧ (transferEff h50t.kern 0 2).Usable 2 ∧
    ¬ NoLocalSelfLock h50t.kern 0 2 ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, pt 0, lf, pt 2, lf], .derive 2 [4] .modify, .store 3 1,
      .transfer 0 2] :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- State after the first five steps of `fao`, the arena created and nothing issued (§57). -/
def h50i : LState := final K0 [] (fao.take 5)

/-- **H50**, `issue` part (material §1 I, class Lib). A block issued into a leaf of its own region
(`issue(0, [5], 5)`, the region available). Historical expected verdict (material): to arbitrate;
under spec v0 a **MISMATCH** in form (obtained `reject`). New expected verdict (spec v0.1, by
arbitration the obtained one): `reject`, decided by §77.2 (local self-blocking prevention, §88).
Obtained: `reject`, static, by local self-blocking prevention alone: the other static
preconditions hold and the destination is in the region. Twin, the same issue into the value 2:
`ok`. -/
theorem H50_issue : RunsTo K0 [] (fao.take 5) h50i ∧ IssueD K0 0 [5] 5 h50i .reject ∧
    OptP (h50i.arenas[0]?) (fun E => IssueStaticBut h50i.kern E [5] 5 ∧
      ¬ IssueStatic h50i.kern E [5] 5) False ∧
    Runs K0 [] (fao.take 5 ++ [.issue 0 [5] 2]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [5] 5) (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Prefix of H51 (§72, §71): frame 1 with allocator 0, `v` (1) and `u` (2), written; storage 3
(element 4) owned by `v`, its root authority 3 held by `v`. -/
def h51p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .write 2 [2],
  .alloc 0 1 [lf, pt 3]]
/-- Run of H51, direct form (§60): 4, `Observe` on `v`. -/
def h51no : List Op := h51p ++ [.derive 1 [1] .observe]
/-- State reached by `h51no` (§57). -/
def h51n : LState := final K0 [] h51no
/-- Run of H51 through a helper (§60, §65, §62): 4, `Modify` on the element, held by the frame;
5, `Observe` on `v`, stored into the element; the helper released. -/
def h51o : List Op := h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .derive 1 [1] .observe, .store 5 4,
  .release 4]
/-- State reached by `h51o` (§57). -/
def h51 : LState := final K0 [] h51o

/-- **H51** (material §1 I, class N3). An element of a storage owned by `v` holds a view on `v`.
Historical expected verdict (material): to arbitrate; under spec v0 a **MISMATCH** in form
(obtained `reject` / `ok`). New expected verdicts (spec v0.1, by arbitration the obtained ones),
decided by §65.2, §67.1, §62.2, §69.1 and §88, clauses v0.1 leaves unchanged: the direct `store`
is `reject`: the view takes away the frame's `Modify` on `v`, hence on the storage it owns (§43
case 4, §65.2, §65.5); twin with the view on another value `u`: `ok`. Through a helper on the
element, then its `release`, the configuration is reached (`ok`); then `v` can be neither written,
nor relieved of the view, nor ended (`reject`, §67.1, §62.2, §69.1), while the view stays
exercisable in `Observe`; the exit of the frame is `ok` (§88: residual blocking). Obtained: the
same. Twins of these three rejections: the same sequence without the view on `v` (its `derive`
and its `store`), then the write of `v` through its root, `ok`, or its `endUse`, `ok`; the same
sequence without the `store` of the view, then its `release`, `ok`. With only the `store` dropped,
the write and the `endUse` stay `reject` for a different cause: the view, then held by the frame,
is active on `v` (§43 case 4, §67.1, §69.1) and releasable. -/
theorem H51 : RunsTo K0 [] h51no h51n ∧ StoreStep 4 4 h51n.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 2 [2] .observe, .store 4 4]) ∧
    RunsTo K0 [] h51o h51 ∧ (∀ a, Write3Step a [1] h51.kern .reject) ∧
    ReleaseStep 5 h51.kern .reject ∧ EndUseStep K0 1 h51.kern .reject ∧
    h51.kern.ExercisableAt 5 .observe ∧ Runs K0 [] (h51o ++ [.exit]) ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .release 4, .write 1 [1]]) ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .derive 1 [1] .observe, .release 4, .release 5]) ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h51p ++ [.derive 3 [4] .modify, .release 4, .endUse 1]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide),
    write_rejected (by decide), .reject (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide,
-----

(fields 3 to 8); storage 9 (leaves 10, 11, 12) owned by 0, `internal` 3; blocks 4, 5, 6 issued
into the fields 3, 4, 5; views 7, 8, 9, `Observe` on the blocks, stored into the fields 6, 7, 8. -/
def w3o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2, pt 2], .write 1 [1],

/-- **W3** (material §5b, frame arena; class Lib, not given by the material). `alloc`,
`newArena`, three `issue`, three views stored into a local structure; `reset` while the views
live; `endUse` of the structure; `reset`; reissue. The material does not say which values hold the
blocks; by arbitration the case issues them into fields of the structure (the literal reading,
blocks issued to separate locals, kept `reset` `reject` after the `endUse` of the structure: a case
defect under spec v0). Expected (material): `reset` during the views `reject`; after `endUse` of
the structure `ok`; reissue `ok`. Obtained: the same (§78.2; §69 effect: the `endUse` of the
structure ends the blocks and the views it holds; §77). Twin of the `reject`: the `endUse` of the
structure, then `reset`, `ok`. -/

I checked all three findings against spec v0.1, the arbitration file, the original brief and the code. All three are real, and I applied each one as a docstring-only change. I rejected one sub-claim of finding 2 (that MM23-H16 needs an extra open-boundary or arbitration classification), with the reason given under open. No theorem statement, proof, definition or model module changed.

Checks:
- `lake build Ern.Corpus.Runner Ern.Corpus.MM3H Ern.Corpus.MM23H Ern.Corpus.MM2H` succeeds (21 jobs) with 0 warnings.
- axcheck.sh reports no axiom outside propext and Quot.sound for all four modules (Runner 94, MM3H 51, MM23H 52 and MM2H 49 theorems).
- The three owned files contain no sorry, admit, native_decide, axiom, noncomputable or set_option.
- Nothing is committed.

Finding 1 (H49 source, MM3H.lean:761-778). Q21 fixed "verdict = verdict obtenu" while the obtained outcome was still the spec v0 one: endUse 2 and endUse 3 `ok`, then `reset` `reject` (blocking report B14). The `endUse` `reject` comes from the v0.1 §69.2 amendment (last sentence, the Q9 follow-up). The docstring now says:
- Q21 keeps H49 as a regression test, with the v0 outcome as its baseline.
- The new verdict is derived from the v0.1 text, not from the obtained outcome.
- The cycle and the `reset` `reject` match that baseline.
- The two `endUse` steps are `reject`, against the baseline's `ok`, decided by v0.1 §69.2, which overrides the baseline for those two steps.

Finding 2 (attribution, MM23H.lean:35 and :815). Obligation 4 of the user's original brief (SP/brief.md) says: "a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves". Both places now say "a decision of the user's brief", not "a decision of the reconstruction".

Finding 3 (H16 twin list, MM3H.lean header). H16's twin removes only `.free 3 7` from h16o ++ [.read 3 [3]], so it is a literal one-step twin. I removed H16 from the list of twins with a faulty element of several steps.

/Users/guygouri/Devlab/ernlang/ern/formal/Ern/Corpus/MM3H.lean: module header no longer lists H16 among twins with a faulty element of several steps (its twin drops the single `free`)

open: Finding 2, sub-claim rejected (MM23-H16 has no open-boundary or arbitration classification). The header says a case whose expected verdict has no v0.1 source is 'kept with its expected verdict and classified'. Here 'classified' means the material rule 5 class, and H16 has one: class R. Its expected verdict has a stated source: the material ('the lowest address among the nonempty leaves') plus the user's brief obligation 4. Obligation 7 of the same brief also says 'MM23-H15 and H16 must now pass'. No arbitration (Q20, Q22) classifies H16, and the case passes. Inventing an open-boundary class for it would be an unrequested interpretation.
